new_entities.name: Cognitive behavioral therapy for social anxiety disorder
new_entities.description: Cognitive behavioral psychotherapy, including exposure-based formats, for social anxiety disorder.

new_entities.name: Social anxiety severity
new_entities.description: The clinical severity of social anxiety symptoms measured using standard disorder-specific scales.

edges.effect_quant: Across placebo-controlled anxiety-disorder trials, CBT shows small-to-moderate benefits for social anxiety disorder. A disorder-specific meta-analysis of internet CBT found a moderate effect versus controls (g -0.55), while a randomized trial of individual and group CBT both improved primary social anxiety symptoms relative to waitlist.
edges.population: adults and young adults with social anxiety disorder in face-to-face or internet-delivered CBT trials
edges.mechanism: CBT for social anxiety targets threat predictions about scrutiny, avoidance of feared situations, and post-event rumination. Exposure practice and cognitive restructuring reduce the perceived danger of social evaluation, which tends to lower overall symptom severity.
edges.summary: The literature supports CBT as a real treatment for social anxiety, but the effect is more often moderate than dramatic. Different formats appear helpful, and internet-delivered CBT can approach face-to-face outcomes in selected settings.
edges.caveats: Some trials focus on internet or group delivery rather than classic individual CBT, and effect sizes in social anxiety tend to be smaller than in disorders such as OCD or GAD. Treatment engagement and exposure completion remain important moderators.

evidence.citation: GuoS et al 2021 Clin Psychol Psychother
evidence.notes: The efficacy of internet-based cognitive behavioural therapy for social anxiety disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
